*** Add File: Strategy_Loop.md
+# DWS IQ Intelligence Growth Strategy Loop
+
+***
+
+# VERSION AND AGENT HISTORY
+
+Version: 1.0
+
+Sessions & Modifications:
+
+- Version: 1.0 | Tool: GitHub Copilot CLI (GPT-5.6 Sol) | Session: dbab1ef1-b889-481d-bd82-b8485342d40d | Date: 05.08.2026 | Changes: Initial research note defining the research question, intelligence maturity model, evidence gate, growth loop, and product-line disposition.
+
+Session Links & References:
+
+- Repository: https://github.com/blogtheristo/dws6
+
+Document Status:
+
+- Created: 05.08.2026
+- Last Modified: 05.08.2026
+- Language: English
+- Publication Status: DRAFT
+- Document Type: Internal Research Note / Product Strategy
+- Owner: Risto Anton Päärni, Founder, CEO, Lifetime Oy
+
+***
+
+## Executive decision
+
+DWS IQ should become an **enterprise research-and-decision system**, not a broad catalog of AI services.
+
+“Doctorate-level” and “post-doctorate-level” must describe observable system behavior, not model branding:
+
+- **Doctorate-level intelligence:** answers a difficult, bounded enterprise question through an explicit method; uses traceable evidence; states assumptions and uncertainty; and survives independent reproduction, domain-expert review, and audit.
+- **Post-doctorate-level intelligence:** identifies a material question the enterprise has not yet framed; proposes competing hypotheses; designs governed tests, simulations, or counterfactual analyses; produces new validated industrial knowledge; and converts the finding into a governed decision or customer-owned capability.
+
+> **Growth thesis:** DWS IQ grows when each customer decision improves the governed intelligence system, and each validated learning becomes reusable Customer-Retained Capital without leaking customer-confidential knowledge.
+
+The product-line test is:
+
+> **Does the offer produce an audit-surviving decision, improve a governed knowledge asset, or directly enable those outcomes in a way the enterprise can inspect?**
+
+## 1. Research basis
+
+External evidence shows a gap between AI adoption and enterprise value:
+
+- Stanford HAI reported that 78% of surveyed organizations used AI in 2024 and 71% used generative AI in at least one function. Reported financial gains were usually modest, while formal responsible-AI evaluation remained uncommon.
+- McKinsey's 2025 global survey reported 88% AI use in at least one function, but only 23% were scaling agentic AI somewhere in the enterprise and 39% reported measurable enterprise-level EBIT impact.
+- NIST AI RMF and its Generative AI Profile organize trustworthy deployment around **Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage**. DWS IQ must expose all four as product behavior.
+- EU AI Act Articles 12 and 14 make logging and effective human oversight central for high-risk systems. Intelligence that cannot show its evidence, interventions, overrides, and operational history is unsuitable for regulated decisions.
+- OECD work on AI-supported evaluation emphasizes evidence quality, methodological rigor, governance, and the limits of automated causal interpretation.
+
+**Conclusion:** enterprise buyers will not believe a doctorate-level claim because DWS has many agents, skills, models, or benchmarks. They will believe it when DWS demonstrates a repeatable chain from question to evidence to governed decision to measured outcome to retained knowledge.
+
+## 2. Primary Research Question
+
+### RQ0 — Intelligence growth
+
+> **How can DWS IQ transform enterprise data, regulatory evidence, domain ontologies, and human expertise into reproducible, audit-grade decisions and novel validated industrial knowledge that measurably increases Monthly Governed Decisions and Customer-Retained Capital across regulated industries while preserving sovereignty, confidentiality, and effective human oversight?**
+
+### Falsifiable hypothesis
+
+> Enterprises using the DWS IQ intelligence loop will produce more audit-surviving governed decisions, in less decision-cycle time and with better calibrated confidence, while retaining more reusable knowledge capital than comparable expert-only, generic-copilot, or ungoverned-agent workflows.
+
+The hypothesis fails if DWS IQ cannot outperform an agreed baseline on decision quality, cycle time, auditability, or retained knowledge after accounting for cost and human-review effort.
+
+## 3. Questions DWS must answer
+
+### Enterprise problem and buyer
+
+1. Which recurring decisions create the greatest regulatory, operational, safety, revenue, or capital-allocation value in each industry?
+2. Which role owns each decision, supplies evidence, can veto it, and signs the economic case?
+3. What proof must R03/R04 research leaders, R13/R15 technical approvers, and R22/R23 executive sponsors see before they call DWS IQ intelligent?
+4. Which decisions are repeated and data-rich enough to become products rather than consulting projects?
+
+### Knowledge and evidence
+
+5. What minimum ontology, evidence, temporal context, and customer knowledge does each decision require?
+6. How will every material claim link to a source, observation, rule, calculation, or expert judgment?
+7. How will DWS distinguish fact, inference, hypothesis, simulation, and recommendation?
+8. Which learning may generalize across customers, and which must remain tenant-private?
+
+### Reasoning and discovery
+
+9. Can DWS compare competing hypotheses rather than produce one plausible narrative?
+10. Can it perform scenario, sensitivity, causal, and counterfactual analysis where needed?
+11. Can it identify missing evidence and design the next cheapest useful observation or experiment?
+12. Can it discover and prospectively validate a previously unknown regulatory, operational, supply-chain, or commercial relationship?
+
+### Evaluation and scientific quality
+
+13. What expert-created gold cases represent real enterprise difficulty rather than demo difficulty?
+14. How reproducible is an answer across models, runs, data perturbations, and reviewers?
+15. Are confidence estimates calibrated against observed correctness and outcomes?
+16. What are the rates of unsupported claims, evidence omissions, tool failures, planning failures, and human overrides?
+17. Does the product outperform the current workflow on quality, time, cost, risk removed, and capital retained?
+
+### Governance and enterprise trust
+
+18. Can an auditor reconstruct each claim, its evidence, model, tool, and human action?
+19. Can the enterprise set decision rights, autonomy limits, stop conditions, data boundaries, and escalation rules?
+20. Can DWS prove sovereignty and confidentiality across the complete model, tool, logging, and support chain?
+21. How are model, regulation, data, and ontology drift detected before they change a decision?
+
+### Learning and economics
+
+22. Which outcomes increase Monthly Governed Decisions (MGD), and which create Customer-Retained Capital (CRC)?
+23. How does one validated customer learning become a reusable evaluation, ontology pattern, skill, or workflow without exposing confidential data?
+24. What is the marginal cost and latency of each governed decision, including human review?
+25. Which improvements increase renewal, expansion, and cross-industry transfer rather than feature count?
+26. Which offers cannot accumulate intelligence and should be separated, bundled, or retired?
+
+## 4. Intelligence maturity model
+
+| Level | Name | Observable behavior | Enterprise proof |
+|---:|---|---|---|
+| 0 | Utility | Executes a fixed task | Successful completion |
+| 1 | Assistant | Retrieves, drafts, or summarizes | Sources and human acceptance |
+| 2 | Specialist | Applies bounded domain rules and tools | Domain test set and expert review |
+| 3 | Governed decision intelligence | Recommends with evidence, uncertainty, lineage, controls, and HIC approval | Audit replay, calibrated evaluation, measured outcome |
+| 4 | Doctorate-level intelligence | Frames and answers a difficult bounded question through a reproducible method | Independent reproduction, adversarial review, expert baseline |
+| 5 | Post-doctorate-level intelligence | Generates and validates a novel hypothesis that changes enterprise action or knowledge | Prospective validation and reusable customer-owned knowledge |
+
+Only Levels 3–5 belong in the flagship DWS IQ Intelligence line. Levels 0–2 may remain components or onboarding services, but must not headline the intelligence claim.
+
+## 5. Intelligence Product Gate
+
+Every flagship product must pass ten gates:
+
+1. **Decision:** names the high-value enterprise decision it improves.
+2. **Owner:** names the accountable role and HIC intervention point.
+3. **Evidence:** returns claim-level provenance and evidence coverage.
+4. **Method:** exposes assumptions, calculations, alternatives, and reasoning method.
+5. **Uncertainty:** provides calibrated confidence and abstention/escalation behavior.
+6. **Evaluation:** has expert gold cases, adversarial cases, repeat-run reliability, and a baseline.
+7. **Governance:** provides Article 12-grade lineage, audit replay, access control, and Article 14 oversight.
+8. **Learning:** detects drift and turns approved outcomes into governed reusable knowledge.
+9. **Economics:** measures cycle time, risk removed, financial effect, MGD, and CRC.
+10. **Visibility:** exposes an evidence graph, decision replay, evaluation card, and outcome dashboard.
+
+Score each gate 0–3: absent, claimed, demonstrated, independently validated. Passing requires no zero, production proof for Gates 1, 3, 6, 7, and 9, and at least 24/30.
+
+## 6. Strategy loop
+
+1. **Observe:** capture a real decision, outcome, failure, regulation, signal, or expert correction.
+2. **Question:** formulate the decision question and competing hypotheses.
+3. **Map:** bind roles, ontology, evidence, controls, and economic value.
+4. **Evaluate first:** define gold cases, failure cases, baseline, threshold, and stop conditions.
+5. **Run:** execute with claim-level evidence and uncertainty.
+6. **HIC decision:** approve, override, request evidence, or stop.
+7. **Measure:** record quality, cycle time, review effort, economic effect, MGD, and CRC.
+8. **Learn:** convert approved learning into an evaluation case, ontology update, skill, policy, or threshold.
+9. **Productize:** expose the capability through product, API/CLI, MCP, dashboard, and audit pack.
+10. **Scale:** sell the proven decision to the next role, site, business unit, or industry.
+
+Cadence:
+
+- Weekly: inspect failures, overrides, drift, and unsupported claims.
+- Monthly: rank improvements by MGD, CRC, renewal evidence, and evaluation lift.
+- Quarterly: gate every SKU and promote, reposition, bundle, sunset, or retire.
+- Annually: independently reproduce Level 4–5 claims and publish a customer-safe evidence report.
+
+## 7. Enterprise-visible proof
+
+Create one **DWS IQ Intelligence Evidence Room** containing:
+
+- decision maps by role and industry;
+- claim-to-source evidence graphs;
+- complete governed-decision replays;
+- model/tool/version lineage and human interventions;
+- confidence calibration and known failure modes;
+- gold-case and adversarial evaluation results;
+- cycle-time and financial baseline comparisons;
+- MGD and CRC trends;
+- ontology growth and drift history;
+- validated discoveries with novelty and validation clearly separated;
+- one redacted customer case from question to retained knowledge.
+
+This replaces agent count, skill count, token throughput, and model leaderboards as the primary proof of intelligence.
+
+## 8. Product-line disposition
+
+### 8.1 Retain and upgrade through the gate
+
+- DWS IQ Platform, Climate Intelligence, Aegis, Compliance Agent, SiteSense, Material Oracle, Emissions Data, Schedule Genius, Construction Agent, Logistics, Sovereignty Monitor, Quality Gate, Viability, Themis, and T3/T4 function bundles.
+- Industry Pods and LWM Industry Ontologies when ontology depth is connected to evaluated decisions.
+- DWS IQ Report, Firehorse Amplify, Content Management/Evidence Vault, and Signed Reports when bundled as evidence, execution, or assurance components.
+- Outcome-priced compliance gaps, site-safety assessments, LCA reports, and applied-AI pilots when acceptance criteria and measured outcomes are explicit.
+
+### 8.2 Offers that do not meet the flagship strategy as currently sold
+
+These may still be useful businesses. They fail because they sell generic labor, training, commodity implementation, infrastructure, content, or task automation without independently visible governed intelligence.
+
+#### Remove from the DWS IQ line, separate, or sunset
+
+| SKU | Offer | Gap | Action |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `professional-web-pages` | Atk-apu pk-yritykselle | General IT support and websites | Sunset or move outside DWS IQ |
+| `secure-email-proton` | Protonmail implementation | Commodity implementation | Move to partner/referral catalog |
+| `m365-consultancy` | Microsoft 365 Agent Consultancy | Tool-specific implementation | Repackage around a governed DWS workflow |
+| `digital-design-gold` | Digital Design Gold | Brand-content production | Separate Firehorse creative service |
+| `cloud-ready-teams` | On-demand engineers | Staff augmentation | Remove from core catalog |
+| `business-mentor-30` | AI Strategy mentoring | Generic and non-reproducible | Replace with a decision-specific research sprint |
+| `FLEET-VIP-001` | Lifetime VIP AI Services | Mobility mixed with edge robotics | Split; remove mobility from DWS IQ |
+
+#### Infrastructure enablers, not intelligence products
+
+Keep only beneath a named, evaluated decision product:
+
+- `edge-node-gn100`, `LF-SITROOM-001`, `LF-COMPLIANCE-AMBULANCE-001`
+- `LF-NVIDIA-INSTALL`, `LF-JETSON-NANO`, `LF-JETSON-AGX`, `LF-DGX-SPARK`, `LF-JETSON-NX`, `LF-IGX-ORIN`
+- `DWS-SOVEREIGN-DB-001`, `sovereignty-cloud-consulting`, `AIS-EU-SOV-OC`, `aws-consultancy`
+
+Hardware specifications, migration completion, or CLOUD Act positioning alone do not demonstrate doctorate-level intelligence.
+
+#### Adoption services, not intelligence products
+
+Attach these to a Level 3–5 product rather than presenting them as flagship intelligence:
+
+- `firehorse-coach`, `ai-koulutus-3d`
+- `claude-code-coaching-3day`, `claude-code-coaching-lecture`, `claude-code-coaching-workshop`, `claude-code-coaching-project`
+- `consulting-hourly`, `consulting-fit55`, `ai-agent-engineering`
+- `lean-project`, `ai-consultant-day`, `ai-consulting-agentic`
+
+The `LAND-*` offers have the better pattern because they attach enablement to a 12-month agent product. Measure the resulting MGD and CRC.
+
+#### Generic assistants and growth tools requiring research-grade upgrades
+
+| SKU/family | Gap | Required upgrade |
+|---|---|---|
+| `conversational-agent` | Channel deployment is not intelligence | Bind to a domain decision, evidence graph, abstention policy, and evaluation |
+| `firehorse-flow` | Optimization asserted without method | Add controlled experiments, causal attribution, confidence, and economics |
+| `omnichannel-multimodal`, `FH-OMNI-001` | May optimize proxy metrics | Add hypotheses, incrementality testing, and governed claims |
+| `CSAT-T1/T2` | Descriptive sentiment/churn | Prospectively validate indicators and retained-revenue interventions |
+| `LF-T1/T2` | Feedback summarization | Convert feedback into tested product hypotheses |
+| `CS-T1/T2` | Monitoring without decision proof | Add materiality, scenarios, prediction tracking, and decision impact |
+| `SEO-T1/T2` | Narrow channel utility | Separate or connect to causal commercial experiments |
+| `DW-T1/T2` | Repository extraction utility | Use beneath governed engineering decisions |
+| `FH-CMS-001` | Evidence storage/search | Add contradiction, expiry-impact, quality, and decision lineage |
+| `FH-SIGN-001` | Signature assurance | Keep as governed-artifact add-on |
+| `firehorse-data-services` | Broad promise | Replace with a bounded data-to-decision product |
+| `devops-lead` | Hidden assessment method | Publish scoring, evidence, sensitivity, baseline, and outcome |
+
+#### Strategic inconsistencies
+
+- `DWS-US-STARTER` and `DWS-US-PILOT` weaken the Sovereign Industrial Intelligence narrative. Keep only as explicitly non-sovereign evaluation tiers with mandatory migration paths.
+- The DWS IQ Platform description currently leads with fleet size, ontology classes, captain hats, and a “90% reduction” claim. Rewrite it around audited decisions, CRC, evidence quality, and measured outcomes.
+- The catalog has grown far beyond the Product Standard's historical “30-product rule.” Breadth now risks making DWS appear to be a marketplace of unrelated services rather than one compounding intelligence system.
+
+## 9. Recommended architecture
+
+1. **DWS IQ Intelligence Core** — governed decision engine, evidence graph, evaluation system, HIC controls, MGD/CRC.
+2. **Intelligence Functions** — Compliance, ESG, HSE, Construction, Sovereignty, Commercial/GTM, and Themis.
+3. **Industry Research Pods** — industry ontology, evaluations, regulatory models, and validated discoveries.
+4. **Deployment and Adoption** — sovereign cloud/edge, integrations, training, implementation, and signed evidence; never presented as the intelligence itself.
+
+> One intelligence core, multiple enterprise functions, industry-specific research depth, and optional sovereign deployment.
+
+## 10. First 90-day research programme
+
+### Days 1–30 — define and baseline
+
+- Select one compliance, one operational/safety, and one commercial decision.
+- Assign enterprise owners and HIC roles.
+- Build 30–50 expert gold cases per decision, including adversarial and abstention cases.
+- Measure the human-only or generic-copilot baseline.
+
+### Days 31–60 — demonstrate doctorate-level behavior
+
+- Implement claim-level evidence, explicit assumptions, competing hypotheses, calibrated confidence, and audit replay.
+- Run repeatability, perturbation, cross-model, and expert-review tests.
+- Publish internal evaluation cards with failures included.
+
+### Days 61–90 — test post-doctorate-level behavior
+
+- Ask each workflow to identify one high-value unknown.
+- Require an experiment, simulation, prospective prediction, or evidence-collection plan.
+- Validate at least one hypothesis against later evidence or operational results.
+- Convert it into customer-owned ontology/evaluation capital.
+- Publish a redacted Intelligence Evidence Room and reposition the first non-aligned SKUs.
+
+## 11. Success criteria
+
+The strategy works when MGD and CRC grow; evidence coverage and calibration improve; unsupported claims and overrides decline; cycle time and review effort fall; at least one validated discovery per quarter changes an enterprise decision; and core recurring revenue grows faster than stand-alone services.
+
+It is not working if growth is explained mainly by more agents, SKUs, pilots, model calls, or consulting hours.
+
+## 12. HIC decision point
+
+**Q1 — Portfolio gate (RECOMMEND: APPROVE)**  
+**Decision owner:** Risto Anton Päärni, Founder, CEO (R22)  
+**Reversibility:** Two-way door; the gate can be revised after quarterly evidence.  
+**Verified basis:** Current catalog, DWS MGD/CRC doctrine, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act Articles 12/14, Stanford HAI, McKinsey, and OECD sources listed below.  
+**Proposed action:** From Q4 2026, no offer headlines DWS IQ Intelligence unless it passes Level 3. Level 4–5 claims require an evaluation card and independent review. Other offers are labeled Deployment, Adoption, Infrastructure, or Services.  
+**Answer format:** `Q1 APPROVE` or `Q1 REJECT — <reason>`.
+
+## Sources
+
+1. NIST, *AI Risk Management Framework* and *Generative AI Profile*: https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework and https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence
+2. Stanford HAI, *2025 AI Index — Economy*: https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/economy
+3. Stanford HAI, *2025 AI Index — Responsible AI*: https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/responsible-ai
+4. McKinsey, *The State of AI: Global Survey 2025*: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai
+5. McKinsey, *From promise to impact*: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/from-promise-to-impact-how-companies-can-measure-and-realize-the-full-value-of-ai
+6. European Commission AI Act Service Desk, Articles 12 and 14: https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-12 and https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-14
+7. OECD, *AI in policy evaluation*: https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/governing-with-artificial-intelligence_795de142-en/full-report/ai-in-policy-evaluation_c88cc2fd.html
+8. OECD, *AI Principles*: https://www.oecd.org/en/topics/ai-principles.html
+9. Internal sources: `DWS_TRUTH_STANDARD.md`, `DWS_PRODUCT_STANDARD.md`, `DWS_MARKET_RESEARCH_STANDARD.md`, `DWS_ROLES_REGISTRY.md`, `AI_AGENT_GUIDELINES.md`, `config/truth/mgd-crc-metrics.json`, and `dws10.com/config/products.json`.
+
+***

You are the GitHub Copilot CLI, a terminal assistant built by GitHub. You are an interactive CLI tool that helps users with software engineering tasks.

# Tone and style
* After completing a task, make the outcome clear, explain the meaningful change, and mention a next step only when it is necessary. End once the requested result is delivered. Do not add a recap, optional extras, an offer to continue, or a follow-up question.
* Lead with the outcome. Start with the main result or answer, then add the most important supporting detail.
* Prefer concise, information-dense prose. Do not repeat the user's request, and cut filler, recap, and obvious process narration.
* Match the amount of detail to the work. Stay terse for straightforward confirmations; add explanation for fixes, investigations, tradeoffs, or real uncertainty. Do the validation needed, but don't mention it unless the user explicitly asked for it. Do not note the validation, verification, tests, checks, in the final response.
* If something is incomplete, uncertain, or blocked, say that plainly instead of claiming completion first.
* Use GitHub-flavored Markdown. Default to the shortest response that still fully answers the request: usually 1-2 short paragraphs, not sections. Use **bold** for labels and emphasis.
* Use lists sparingly and **only** when separate items are genuinely easier to scan than short prose. For numbered lists, only use the '1. 2. 3.' style markers (with a period). **Never** use nested lists, and consider merging small items to a single line.
* Consider a markdown table instead of bullet lists with inline labels.
* Keep the tone collaborative, direct, and natural, like a concise handoff to a teammate.
* Leave a blank line between paragraphs.

# Search and delegation
* When prompting sub-agents, provide comprehensive context — brevity rules do not apply to sub-agent prompts.
* When searching the file system for files or text, stay in the current working directory or child directories of the cwd unless absolutely necessary.
* When searching code, the preference order for tools to use is: code intelligence tools (if available) > LSP-based tools (if available) > glob > rg with glob pattern > bash tool.

**Session database** (database: "session", the default):
The per-session database persists across the session but is isolated from other sessions.

**When to use SQL vs plan.md:**
- Use plan.md for prose: problem statements, approach notes, high-level planning
- Use SQL for operational data: todo lists, test cases, batch items, status tracking

**Pre-existing tables (ready to use):**
- `todos`: id, title, description, status (pending/in_progress/done/blocked), created_at, updated_at
- `todo_deps`: todo_id, depends_on (for dependency tracking)

**Todo tracking workflow:**
Use descriptive kebab-case IDs (not t1, t2). Write titles in gerund form (e.g. "Creating user auth module"). Include enough detail that the todo can be executed without referring back to the plan:
```sql
INSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES
  ('user-auth', 'Creating user auth module', 'Implement JWT auth in src/auth/ so login, logout, and token refresh don''t depend on server sessions. Use bcrypt for password hashing.');
```

**Todo status workflow:**
- `pending`: Todo is waiting to be started
- `in_progress`: You are actively working on this todo (set this before starting!)
- `done`: Todo is complete
- `blocked`: Todo cannot proceed (document why in description)

**IMPORTANT: Always update todo status as you work:**
1. Before starting a todo: `UPDATE todos SET status = 'in_progress' WHERE id = 'X'`
2. After completing a todo: `UPDATE todos SET status = 'done' WHERE id = 'X'`
3. Check todo_status in each user message to see what's ready

**Dependencies:** Insert into todo_deps when one todo must complete before another:
```sql
INSERT INTO todo_deps (todo_id, depends_on) VALUES ('api-routes', 'user-model');  -- routes wait for model
```

**Create any tables you need.** The database is yours to use for any purpose:
- Load and query data (CSVs, API responses, file listings)
- Track progress on batch operations
- Store intermediate results for multi-step analysis
- Any workflow where SQL queries would help

Common patterns:

1. **Todo tracking with dependencies:**
```sql
-- todos and todo_deps already exist — do NOT CREATE them, just INSERT:
INSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES ('user-model', 'Creating user model', 'Define the User schema and relations in src/models/user.ts');

-- Find todos with no pending dependencies ("ready" query):
SELECT t.* FROM todos t
WHERE t.status = 'pending'
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM todo_deps td
    JOIN todos dep ON td.depends_on = dep.id
    WHERE td.todo_id = t.id AND dep.status != 'done'
);
```

2. **TDD test case tracking:**
```sql
CREATE TABLE test_cases (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT DEFAULT 'not_written'
);
SELECT * FROM test_cases WHERE status = 'not_written' LIMIT 1;
UPDATE test_cases SET status = 'written' WHERE id = 'tc1';
```

3. **Batch item processing (e.g., PR comments):**
```sql
CREATE TABLE review_items (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    file_path TEXT,
    comment TEXT,
    status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending'
);
SELECT * FROM review_items WHERE status = 'pending' AND file_path = 'src/auth.ts';
UPDATE review_items SET status = 'addressed' WHERE id IN ('r1', 'r2');
```

4. **Session state (key-value):**
```sql
CREATE TABLE session_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO session_state (key, value) VALUES ('current_phase', 'testing');
SELECT value FROM session_state WHERE key = 'current_phase';
```

**When to Use Sub-Agents**
* Use a matching specialist when the request specifically calls for that domain expertise.
* For other reviews, audits, and summaries, never delegate parts of a codebase that is small enough to read directly, regardless of how it divides into separate areas; do them yourself. Never delegate passes over the same files; delegate only work that needs separate context.

**When to use explore agent** (not rg/glob):
* Never use explore to split a review, audit, or summary by labeled area when its total scope is small; do it yourself. Reserve explore for independent threads that need substantial separate context.
* For simple lookups — understanding a specific component, finding a symbol, or reading a few known files — do it yourself using rg/glob/view. This is faster and keeps context in your conversation.
* Trace a single continuous chain yourself.
* Do not speculatively launch explore agents in the background "just in case" — they consume resources and rarely finish before you've already found the answer yourself.

**If you do use explore:**
* The explore agent is stateless — provide complete context in each call.
* Batch related questions into one call. Launch independent explorations in parallel.
* Do NOT duplicate its work by calling rg/view on files it already reported.
* Once you have enough information to address the user's request, stop investigating and deliver the result. Don't chase every lead or do redundant follow-up searches.

**When to use custom agents**:
* If both a built-in agent and a custom agent could handle a task, prefer the custom agent as it has specialized knowledge for this environment.

**How to Use Sub-Agents**
* Instruct the sub-agent to do the task itself, not just give advice.
* Once you delegate a scope to an agent, that agent owns it until it completes or fails; do not investigate the same scope yourself.
* If a sub-agent fails repeatedly, do the task yourself.
**Avoiding Unnecessary Sub-Agent Delegation**
* Before delegating, assess whether a direct approach (1-2 tool calls with rg/glob/view) would be faster. Only delegate tasks that genuinely benefit from multi-step autonomous work.
* If a sub-agent completes with 0 useful turns or produces no actionable output, do not re-launch it — fall back to doing the work yourself immediately.

**Background Agents**
* After launching a background agent for work you need before your next step, tell the user you're waiting, then end your response with no tool calls. A completion notification will arrive automatically.
* When that notification arrives, a good default is to call read_agent once with wait: true to retrieve the result. If it still shows running, stop there for this response. Leave same-scope work with the agent while it runs.
* Use read_agent for completed background agents, not to check whether they're done.

**Multi-Turn Conversations**
* Background agents stay alive after responding. Instead of launching a new agent, send follow-up messages with write_agent to refine, correct, or extend the agent's work.
* Prefer write_agent for iterative refinement over launching a new agent — the agent retains its full conversation context.
* Typical workflow: start agent (background) → wait for completion notification → read_agent (get result) → write_agent (send refinement) → wait for notification → read_agent (get updated result).
* Use read_agent with since_turn as an inclusive 0-based start turn.
* Idle agents (status: "idle") are waiting for messages — they're ready to receive write_agent immediately.

### Issue: TypeScript Build Fails with "Cannot find name 'process'"
**Cause:** Missing @types/node dependency  
**Fix:** Ensure `npm install` was run first. The error appears if you build before installing dependencies.

### Issue: Morning Briefing Runs Twice During DST Transitions
**Cause:** GitHub Actions cron uses UTC, Finland observes DST  
**Fix:** Use dual cron entries with time-guard in script (see `.github/workflows/morning-briefing.yml:6-11`)

### Issue: node-cron Doesn't Work in Serverless (Cloud Run, Scaleway)

## Automated PR Workflow (HIL Automation)

This repo uses a fully automated multi-agent PR workflow that **replaces manual human-in-the-loop review**.

### Flow
1. **Claude Code** generates implementation on a feature branch and opens a draft PR
2. **AI Code Review (HIL)** workflow triggers automatically (`.github/workflows/ai-pr-review.yml`)
   - **Claude** does quick sanity check (security, correctness, breaking changes)
   - **Gemini** does deep HIL review (replaces human reviewer: edge cases, tests, architecture, security audit)
   - Both must approve — Gemini is the mandatory quality gate
   - Posts combined review as PR comment
   - Adds labels: `ai-reviewed` + `ai-approved` or `ai-changes-requested`
3. **If changes requested** (mandatory, not optional): Gemini's required changes + test gaps are formatted as structured @copilot instructions
   - Copilot coding agent picks up the comment and implements fixes autonomously
   - Pushes to the PR branch, re-triggering the review workflow
   - Loop repeats until both reviewers approve (typically 1-3 iterations)
4. **Gemini requests fixes → Copilot implements** (mandatory, not optional): This is the core automation loop
   - Gemini acts as strict senior engineer — flags critical issues, missing tests, edge cases
   - Fix instructions are specific and actionable (file:line references)
   - Copilot implements changes, runs `npm run build` and `npm test`
   - Review re-triggers automatically on push
5. **When approved**: `ai-approved` label triggers auto-merge workflow
   - Verifies all CI checks pass
   - Enables squash auto-merge (or adds `ready-to-merge` label)
6. **Human override**: Add `do-not-merge` or `needs-human-review` labels to pause

| `ai-reviewed` | AI review has been performed (dual-model) |
| `ai-approved` | Both Claude + Gemini approved |
| `ai-changes-requested` | One or both reviewers found issues |
| `ready-to-merge` | All checks passed, safe to merge |
| `do-not-merge` | Blocks auto-merge (human override) |
| `needs-human-review` | Pauses automation for manual review |

### Required Secrets

## 2. Lifetime Scope Signals Protocol

### What Are Lifetime Scope Signals?

Signals are the communication mechanism between agents. When an agent completes a milestone, it **emits** a signal. Other agents **listen** for signals before proceeding with dependent tasks.

### Signal Format

```
[AGENT-XX]:SIGNAL_TYPE:MILESTONE:TIMESTAMP
```

**Components:**

- `AGENT-XX`: Agent identifier (e.g., `AGENT-01`, `AGENT-07`)
- `SIGNAL_TYPE`: `READY`, `COMPLETE`, `ERROR`, `BLOCKED`
- `MILESTONE`: Specific deliverable (e.g., `supabase-auth`, `rls-policies`)
- `TIMESTAMP`: ISO 8601 format

**Examples:**

```
[AGENT-07]:READY:rls-policies:2026-01-05T14:30:00Z
[AGENT-01]:COMPLETE:v1-auth:2026-01-10T09:00:00Z
[AGENT-02]:BLOCKED:report-api:2026-01-06T10:15:00Z
```

### Signal Types

| Type       | Meaning                                          | Action                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `READY`    | Milestone achieved, dependent agents can proceed | Unblocks downstream agents           |
| `COMPLETE` | All agent work finished                          | Agent moves to complete status       |
| `ERROR`    | Agent encountered failure                        | Alerts coordinator, may block others |
| `BLOCKED`  | Agent waiting for external dependency            | No action until unblocked            |

### How Agents Learn Signals

#### Option A: File-Based (Current Implementation)

Agents read from `AGENT_SIGNAL_REGISTRY.json`:

```javascript
// coordinator.cjs
const registry = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("AGENT_SIGNAL_REGISTRY.json"));
const myDependencies = registry.agents["agent-02"].signals.listening;
const emittedSignals = collectEmittedSignals(registry);
const unmet = myDependencies.filter((sig) => !emittedSignals.has(sig));
// If unmet.length === 0, agent can proceed
```

**Commands:**

```bash
cd .workflows/agents
node coordinator.cjs status    # Show all agent statuses
node coordinator.cjs signals   # Show signal log
node coordinator.cjs ready     # Show which agents can launch
node coordinator.cjs emit agent-07 READY:schema-users  # Emit signal
```

#### Option B: MCP Hub Real-Time (Future)

```python
# mcp-hub/server.py addition
@app.post("/signals/emit")
async def emit_signal(agent_id: str, signal: str):
    await supabase.table("agent_signals").insert({...})
    await notify_listeners(agent_id, signal)
```

### Deployment Phases

```yaml
# Phase 1: Silent Pilot (30 days)
mode: "silent_pilot"
actions: ["observe", "generate_reports", "calibrate"]
approval: none
output: "Daily reports to Slack and/or Microsoft Teams"

# Phase 2: Advisor (60 days)
mode: "advisor"
actions: ["recommend", "flag_risks", "suggest_actions"]
approval: required
output: "Recommendations with human approval"

# Phase 3: Autonomous
mode: "autonomous"
actions: ["execute", "send_emails", "create_tasks"]
approval: exception_only
guardrails: ["max_emails", "approval_for_discounts"]
```

### Proactive Agents — Observe → Act (Code Wiring)

The deployment phases above are now enforced in the TypeScript agent runtime via
`AgentConfig.autonomyPhase` (`silent_pilot` | `advisor` | `autonomous`, default
`silent_pilot`). The "observe → act" loop is implemented by:

| Concern                                                    | Module                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| What to watch + 2×2 "worth interrupting" gate              | `src/agents/signal-catalogue.ts`           |
| Phase ladder + comparison                                  | `src/agents/autonomy.ts`                   |
| Nudge chokepoint (dedup, rate limit, escalation, delivery) | `src/agents/nudge.service.ts`              |
| Background observation cron + escalation sweep             | `src/agents/signal-poller.ts`              |
| Confirm / Override / Dismiss / Investigate handling        | `src/agents/nudge-response-handler.ts`     |
| `send_notification` agent tool (KYA phase-gated, BLUE)     | `src/agents/tools.ts`                      |
| Persisted nudge state                                      | `supabase/migrations/069_agent_nudges.sql` |

**Currently promoted to Phase 2 (advisor):** `sitesense`, `compliance`,
`customer-sat`. All other agents remain `silent_pilot` and cannot send nudges.

**Guardrails:** an agent below `advisor` is refused `send_notification` at the
tool gate; nudges are deduplicated per `(orgId, signalKey, entityId)` while
pending, rate-limited per agent (default 5/hour, 20/day, counted from the
persisted table so limits hold across instances), and escalated after a 4h
no-response window via the poller's restart-safe `escalate_at` sweep.

## 8. Managed Agent Backends — Claude Managed Agents vs. DGX Managed Agents

**Terminology.** Two execution substrates exist (or are being evaluated) for running DWS agent workloads:

- **Claude Managed Agents** — Anthropic's hosted agent-execution service (public beta as of this writing, `managed-agents-2026-04-01`). Anthropic runs the session/sandbox/tool loop on its own infrastructure; DWS sends events and receives results. Distinct from the raw Messages API, the Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`, self-hosted loop), and the Claude Agent SDK (self-hosted library) — see Anthropic documentation for the full surface comparison.
- **DGX Managed Agents** (this repo's term for the existing self-hosted substrate) — the Godagent architecture (`docs/Deputy-Agents-Architecture.md`) running on DGX Spark hardware (Acer Veriton GN100, NVIDIA GB10 Superchip, `docs/CLOUD_ENVIRONMENTS.md` §3.2.2), Docker + Dockerode container isolation per tenant/agent, Qwen 2.5 72B primary LLM with Claude Haiku fallback via LiteLLM, orchestrated through `infrastructure/dgx-spark/docker-compose.yml` and the `cron` / `ollama-spark` skills. This is already the platform's primary 24/7 runtime (`Cron-works.md`: 31 daily + 16 weekly jobs).

### 8.1 Comparison

| Dimension                  | Claude Managed Agents                                                                                                               | DGX Managed Agents (current)                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hosting / control plane    | Anthropic-run cloud sandbox by default; a self-hosted-worker mode exists but orchestration still lives on Anthropic's control plane | Fully self-hosted: Docker/Dockerode on Lifetime Oy premises                                                                                    |

**Canonical source.** This is the single home for the 12 engineering-discipline rules. Every agent — Claude Code sessions, subagents, `src/agents/` BaseAgent classes, MCP tools, AgentFoundry, and dev-fleet agents — must have access to these and operate by them. 1. **Think before coding.** State assumptions explicitly; do not guess. The model cannot read your mind — surface what you are assuming before you act.
2. **Simplicity first.** Minimum code, no speculative abstractions. Reject "for future flexibility" additions — they are next quarter's deletions. (Reinforces `/simplify`.)
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task requires. Do not improve adjacent code; unrelated refactors blow up review scope. (Mirrors Non-Negotiable Rule 9.)
4. **Goal-driven execution.** Define success criteria upfront and loop until verified. Without an explicit done-condition an agent either loops forever or stops too early. (Use `/goal`, the verification-gate.)
5. **Use the model only for judgment calls** — classification, drafting, summarization, extraction. NOT routing, retries, status-code handling, or deterministic transforms. If code can answer, code answers.
6. **Token budgets are not advisory.** Per-task 4000, per-session 30000 (`CLAUDE_AUTO_MODE_BUDGET`). Past these, agents re-suggest fixes already rejected. Stop, checkpoint, re-scope.
7. **Surface conflicts, don't average them.** Two patterns in the codebase? Pick one and say why. Blending them swallows errors twice.
8. **Read before you write.** Read exports, callers, and shared utilities first, so you reuse instead of duplicating an identical function you never opened.
9. **Tests verify intent, not just behavior.** A test that cannot fail when business logic changes is wrong. All tests can pass while a function returns a constant — assert the intent.
10. **Checkpoint every significant step.** Commit/verify before building the next step, so step 6 is never stacked on a broken step 4. (Backed by `/ship`, session-stop governance.)
11. **Match the codebase conventions.** Class components stay class components; the established test pattern stays. Do not silently fork a new idiom.
12. **Fail loud.** "Completed successfully" while silently skipping records is the worst class of bug. Surface uncertainty and partial results; never hide them. (Mirrors the hooks' block-don't-ask design.)

5. **Ask the HIC one real, decision-shaped question** — the Article 14 intervention point.
6. **Calendar every dated commitment** — every deadline, expiry, meeting, follow-up or renewal the session produced or discovered, put into Google Calendar in the session that found it (`Google_Calendar.create_event`). See `DWS_LEARNING_STANDARD.md` §4.1.

+- OECD work on AI-supported evaluation emphasizes evidence quality, methodological rigor, governance, and the limits of automated causal interpretation.
+

+
+## 2. Primary Research Question
+
+### RQ0 — Intelligence growth
+
+> **How can DWS IQ transform enterprise data, regulatory evidence, domain ontologies, and human expertise into reproducible, audit-grade decisions and novel validated industrial knowledge that measurably increases Monthly Governed Decisions and Customer-Retained Capital across regulated industries while preserving sovereignty, confidentiality, and effective human oversight?**
+
+### Falsifiable hypothesis
+
+> Enterprises using the DWS IQ intelligence loop will produce more audit-surviving governed decisions, in less decision-cycle time and with better calibrated confidence, while retaining more reusable knowledge capital than comparable expert-only, generic-copilot, or ungoverned-agent workflows.
+
+The hypothesis fails if DWS IQ cannot outperform an agreed baseline on decision quality, cycle time, auditability, or retained knowledge after accounting for cost and human-review effort.
+
+## 3. Questions DWS must answer
+
+### Enterprise problem and buyer
+
+1. Which recurring decisions create the greatest regulatory, operational, safety, revenue, or capital-allocation value in each industry?
+2. Which role owns each decision, supplies evidence, can veto it, and signs the economic case?
+3. What proof must R03/R04 research leaders, R13/R15 technical approvers, and R22/R23 executive sponsors see before they call DWS IQ intelligent?
+4. Which decisions are repeated and data-rich enough to become products rather than consulting projects?
+
+### Knowledge and evidence
+
+5. What minimum ontology, evidence, temporal context, and customer knowledge does each decision require?
+6. How will every material claim link to a source, observation, rule, calculation, or expert judgment?
+7. How will DWS distinguish fact, inference, hypothesis, simulation, and recommendation?
+8. Which learning may generalize across customers, and which must remain tenant-private?
+
+### Reasoning and discovery
+
+9. Can DWS compare competing hypotheses rather than produce one plausible narrative?
+10. Can it perform scenario, sensitivity, causal, and counterfactual analysis where needed?
+11. Can it identify missing evidence and design the next cheapest useful observation or experiment?
+12. Can it discover and prospectively validate a previously unknown regulatory, operational, supply-chain, or commercial relationship?
+
+### Evaluation and scientific quality
+
+13. What expert-created gold cases represent real enterprise difficulty rather than demo difficulty?
+14. How reproducible is an answer across models, runs, data perturbations, and reviewers?
+15. Are confidence estimates calibrated against observed correctness and outcomes?
+16. What are the rates of unsupported claims, evidence omissions, tool failures, planning failures, and human overrides?
+17. Does the product outperform the current workflow on quality, time, cost, risk removed, and capital retained?
+
+### Governance and enterprise trust
+
+18. Can an auditor reconstruct each claim, its evidence, model, tool, and human action?
+19. Can the enterprise set decision rights, autonomy limits, stop conditions, data boundaries, and escalation rules?
+20. Can DWS prove sovereignty and confidentiality across the complete model, tool, logging, and support chain?
+21. How are model, regulation, data, and ontology drift detected before they change a decision?
+
+### Learning and economics
+
+22. Which outcomes increase Monthly Governed Decisions (MGD), and which create Customer-Retained Capital (CRC)?
+23. How does one validated customer learning become a reusable evaluation, ontology pattern, skill, or workflow without exposing confidential data?
+24. What is the marginal cost and latency of each governed decision, including human review?
+25. Which improvements increase renewal, expansion, and cross-industry transfer rather than feature count?
+26. Which offers cannot accumulate intelligence and should be separated, bundled, or retired?
+
+## 4. Intelligence maturity model
+
+| Level | Name | Observable behavior | Enterprise proof |
+|---:|---|---|---|
+| 0 | Utility | Executes a fixed task | Successful completion |
+| 1 | Assistant | Retrieves, drafts, or summarizes | Sources and human acceptance |
+| 2 | Specialist | Applies bounded domain rules and tools | Domain test set and expert review |
+| 3 | Governed decision intelligence | Recommends with evidence, uncertainty, lineage, controls, and HIC approval | Audit replay, calibrated evaluation, measured outcome |
+| 4 | Doctorate-level intelligence | Frames and answers a difficult bounded question through a reproducible method | Independent reproduction, adversarial review, expert baseline |
+| 5 | Post-doctorate-level intelligence | Generates and validates a novel hypothesis that changes enterprise action or knowledge | Prospective validation and reusable customer-owned knowledge |

+2. **Owner:** names the accountable role and HIC intervention point.
+3. **Evidence:** returns claim-level provenance and evidence coverage.

+5. **Uncertainty:** provides calibrated confidence and abstention/escalation behavior.
+6. **Evaluation:** has expert gold cases, adversarial cases, repeat-run reliability, and a baseline.
+7. **Governance:** provides Article 12-grade lineage, audit replay, access control, and Article 14 oversight.
+8. **Learning:** detects drift and turns approved outcomes into governed reusable knowledge.

+2. **Question:** formulate the decision question and competing hypotheses.
+3. **Map:** bind roles, ontology, evidence, controls, and economic value.

+# DWS IQ Intelligence Growth Strategy Loop
+
+***
+
+# VERSION AND AGENT HISTORY
+
+Version: 1.0
+
+Sessions & Modifications:
+
+- Version: 1.0 | Tool: GitHub Copilot CLI (GPT-5.6 Sol) | Session: dbab1ef1-b889-481d-bd82-b8485342d40d | Date: 05.08.2026 | Changes: Initial research note defining the research question, intelligence maturity model, evidence gate, growth loop, and product-line disposition.
+
+Document Status:
+
+- Created: 05.08.2026
+- Last Modified: 05.08.2026
+- Language: English
+- Publication Status: DRAFT
+- Document Type: Internal Research Note / Product Strategy
+- Owner: Risto Anton Päärni, Founder, CEO, Lifetime Oy
+
+***
+
+## Executive decision
+
+DWS IQ should become an **enterprise research-and-decision system**, not a broad catalog of AI services.
+
+“Doctorate-level” and “post-doctorate-level” must describe observable behavior, not model branding:
+
+- **Doctorate-level intelligence:** answers a difficult, bounded enterprise question through an explicit method; uses traceable evidence; states assumptions and uncertainty; and survives independent reproduction, expert review, and audit.
+- **Post-doctorate-level intelligence:** identifies a material question the enterprise has not framed; proposes competing hypotheses; runs governed tests, simulations, or counterfactual analyses; produces new validated industrial knowledge; and converts it into a governed decision or customer-owned capability.
+
+> **Growth thesis:** DWS IQ grows when each customer decision improves the governed intelligence system, and each validated learning becomes reusable Customer-Retained Capital without leaking customer-confidential knowledge.
+
+The product-line test is: **Does the offer produce an audit-surviving decision, improve a governed knowledge asset, or directly enable those outcomes in a way the enterprise can inspect?**
+
+## 1. Research basis
+
+- Stanford HAI reported 78% organizational AI use in 2024 and 71% generative-AI use in at least one function, while financial gains were usually modest and formal responsible-AI evaluation remained uncommon.
+- McKinsey's 2025 survey reported 88% AI use, but only 23% scaling agentic AI somewhere in the enterprise and 39% reporting measurable enterprise-level EBIT impact.
+- NIST AI RMF organizes trustworthy deployment around **Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage**. DWS IQ must expose all four as product behavior.
+- EU AI Act Articles 12 and 14 make logging and effective human oversight central for high-risk systems.
+- OECD work on AI-supported evaluation emphasizes evidence quality, methodological rigor, governance, and the limits of automated causal interpretation.
+
+Enterprise buyers will not believe a doctorate-level claim because DWS has many agents, skills, models, or benchmarks. They will believe a repeatable chain from question to evidence to governed decision to measured outcome to retained knowledge.
+
+## 2. Primary Research Question
+
+> **RQ0: How can DWS IQ transform enterprise data, regulatory evidence, domain ontologies, and human expertise into reproducible, audit-grade decisions and novel validated industrial knowledge that measurably increases Monthly Governed Decisions and Customer-Retained Capital across regulated industries while preserving sovereignty, confidentiality, and effective human oversight?**
+
+### Falsifiable hypothesis
+
+Enterprises using the DWS IQ intelligence loop will produce more audit-surviving governed decisions, in less decision-cycle time and with better calibrated confidence, while retaining more reusable knowledge capital than comparable expert-only, generic-copilot, or ungoverned-agent workflows.
+
+The hypothesis fails if DWS IQ cannot outperform an agreed baseline on decision quality, cycle time, auditability, or retained knowledge after accounting for cost and human-review effort.
+
+## 3. Research questions DWS must answer
+
+### Enterprise value and buyer
+
+1. Which recurring decisions create the greatest regulatory, operational, safety, revenue, or capital-allocation value in each industry?
+2. Which role owns each decision, supplies evidence, can veto it, and signs the economic case?
+3. What proof must R03/R04 research leaders, R13/R15 technical approvers, and R22/R23 executive sponsors see before they call DWS IQ intelligent?
+4. Which decisions are repeated and data-rich enough to become products rather than consulting projects?
+
+### Knowledge and evidence
+
+5. What minimum ontology, evidence, temporal context, and customer knowledge does each decision require?
+6. How will every material claim link to a source, observation, rule, calculation, or expert judgment?
+7. How will DWS distinguish fact, inference, hypothesis, simulation, and recommendation?
+8. Which learning may generalize across customers, and which must remain tenant-private?
+
+### Reasoning and discovery
+
+9. Can DWS compare competing hypotheses rather than produce one plausible narrative?
+10. Can it perform scenario, sensitivity, causal, and counterfactual analysis where needed?
+11. Can it identify missing evidence and design the next cheapest useful observation or experiment?
+12. Can it discover and prospectively validate a previously unknown industrial relationship?
+
+### Evaluation, governance, and economics
+
+13. What expert-created gold cases represent real enterprise difficulty rather than demo difficulty?
+14. How reproducible is an answer across models, runs, data perturbations, and reviewers?
+15. Are confidence estimates calibrated against observed correctness and outcomes?
+16. What are the unsupported-claim, evidence-omission, tool-failure, planning-failure, and human-override rates?
+17. Can an auditor reconstruct each claim, its evidence, model, tool, and human action?
+18. Can the enterprise set autonomy limits, stop conditions, data boundaries, and escalation rules?
+19. How are model, regulation, data, and ontology drift detected before they change a decision?
+20. Which outcomes increase Monthly Governed Decisions (MGD), and which create Customer-Retained Capital (CRC)?
+21. How does approved customer learning become a reusable evaluation, ontology pattern, skill, or workflow without exposing confidential data?
+22. Which offers cannot accumulate intelligence and should be separated, bundled, or retired?
+
+## 4. Intelligence maturity model
+
+| Level | Name | Observable behavior | Enterprise proof |
+|---:|---|---|---|
+| 0 | Utility | Executes a fixed task | Successful completion |
+| 1 | Assistant | Retrieves, drafts, or summarizes | Sources and human acceptance |
+| 2 | Specialist | Applies bounded domain rules and tools | Domain test set and expert review |
+| 3 | Governed decision intelligence | Recommends with evidence, uncertainty, lineage, controls, and HIC approval | Audit replay, calibrated evaluation, measured outcome |
+| 4 | Doctorate-level intelligence | Answers a difficult bounded question through a reproducible method | Independent reproduction, adversarial review, expert baseline |
+| 5 | Post-doctorate-level intelligence | Generates and validates a novel hypothesis that changes enterprise action or knowledge | Prospective validation and reusable customer-owned knowledge |
+
+Only Levels 3–5 belong in the flagship DWS IQ Intelligence line. Levels 0–2 may remain components or onboarding services but must not headline the intelligence claim.
+
+## 5. Intelligence Product Gate
+
+Every flagship product must prove:
+
+1. a named high-value **decision**;
+2. an accountable **owner and HIC intervention point**;
+3. claim-level **evidence and provenance**;
+4. an explicit **method, assumptions, calculations, and alternatives**;
+5. calibrated **uncertainty, abstention, and escalation**;
+6. expert gold cases, adversarial cases, repeatability, and a comparative **evaluation**;
+7. Article 12 lineage, audit replay, access control, and Article 14 **governance**;
+8. drift detection and a governed **learning loop**;
+9. measured cycle time, risk removed, financial effect, MGD, and CRC;
+10. an inspectable evidence graph, decision replay, evaluation card, and outcome dashboard.
+
+Score each gate 0–3: absent, claimed, demonstrated, independently validated. Passing requires no zero, production proof for Gates 1, 3, 6, 7, and 9, and at least 24/30.
+
+## 6. Strategy loop
+
+1. **Observe:** capture a real decision, outcome, failure, regulation, signal, or expert correction.
+2. **Question:** formulate the decision question and competing hypotheses.
+3. **Map:** bind roles, ontology, evidence, controls, and economic value.
+4. **Evaluate first:** define gold cases, failure cases, baseline, threshold, and stop conditions.
+5. **Run:** execute with claim-level evidence and uncertainty.
+6. **HIC decision:** approve, override, request evidence, or stop.
+7. **Measure:** record quality, cycle time, review effort, economic effect, MGD, and CRC.
+8. **Learn:** convert approved learning into an evaluation case, ontology update, skill, policy, or threshold.
+9. **Productize:** expose the capability through product, API/CLI, MCP, dashboard, and audit pack.
+10. **Scale:** sell the proven decision to the next role, site, business unit, or industry.
+
+Review failures weekly, prioritize by MGD/CRC monthly, gate every SKU quarterly, and independently reproduce Level 4–5 claims annually.
+
+## 7. Enterprise-visible proof
+
+Create one **DWS IQ Intelligence Evidence Room** with decision maps, claim-to-source graphs, governed-decision replays, model/tool lineage, human interventions, confidence calibration, known failure modes, evaluation results, baseline comparisons, MGD/CRC trends, ontology drift history, validated discoveries, and a redacted customer case.
+
+This replaces agent count, skill count, token throughput, and model leaderboards as the primary proof of intelligence.
+
+## 8. Product-line disposition
+
+### Retain and upgrade through the gate
+
+- DWS IQ Platform, Climate Intelligence, Aegis, Compliance Agent, SiteSense, Material Oracle, Emissions Data, Schedule Genius, Construction Agent, Logistics, Sovereignty Monitor, Quality Gate, Viability, Themis, and T3/T4 function bundles.
+- Industry Pods and LWM Industry Ontologies when ontology depth is connected to evaluated decisions.
+- DWS IQ Report, Firehorse Amplify, Content Management/Evidence Vault, and Signed Reports when bundled as evidence, execution, or assurance components.
+- Outcome-priced compliance gaps, site-safety assessments, LCA reports, and applied-AI pilots with explicit acceptance criteria.
+
+### Do not meet the flagship strategy as currently sold
+
+#### Remove from the DWS IQ line, separate, or sunset
+
+| SKU | Gap | Action |
+|---|---|---|
+| `professional-web-pages` | General IT support and websites | Sunset or move outside DWS IQ |
+| `secure-email-proton` | Commodity implementation | Move to partner/referral catalog |
+| `m365-consultancy` | Tool-specific implementation | Repackage around a governed DWS workflow |
+| `digital-design-gold` | Brand-content production | Separate Firehorse creative service |
+| `cloud-ready-teams` | Staff augmentation | Remove from core catalog |
+| `business-mentor-30` | Generic, non-reproducible mentoring | Replace with decision-specific research sprint |
+| `FLEET-VIP-001` | Mobility mixed with edge robotics | Split; remove mobility from DWS IQ |
+
+#### Infrastructure enablers, not intelligence products
+
+Keep only beneath a named, evaluated decision product:
+
+- `edge-node-gn100`, `LF-SITROOM-001`, `LF-COMPLIANCE-AMBULANCE-001`
+- `LF-NVIDIA-INSTALL`, `LF-JETSON-NANO`, `LF-JETSON-AGX`, `LF-DGX-SPARK`, `LF-JETSON-NX`, `LF-IGX-ORIN`
+- `DWS-SOVEREIGN-DB-001`, `sovereignty-cloud-consulting`, `AIS-EU-SOV-OC`, `aws-consultancy`
+
+Hardware specifications, migration completion, or CLOUD Act positioning alone do not demonstrate doctorate-level intelligence.
+
+#### Adoption services, not intelligence products
+
+Attach to a Level 3–5 product:
+
+- `firehorse-coach`, `ai-koulutus-3d`
+- `claude-code-coaching-3day`, `claude-code-coaching-lecture`, `claude-code-coaching-workshop`, `claude-code-coaching-project`
+- `consulting-hourly`, `consulting-fit55`, `ai-agent-engineering`
+- `lean-project`, `ai-consultant-day`, `ai-consulting-agentic`
+
+The `LAND-*` offers have the better pattern because they attach enablement to a 12-month agent product. Measure the resulting MGD and CRC.
+
+#### Generic assistants and growth tools requiring upgrade
+
+| SKU/family | Required upgrade |
+|---|---|
+| `conversational-agent` | Domain decision, evidence graph, abstention policy, and evaluation |
+| `firehorse-flow` | Controlled experiments, causal attribution, confidence, and economics |
+| `omnichannel-multimodal`, `FH-OMNI-001` | Hypotheses, incrementality testing, and governed claims |
+| `CSAT-T1/T2` | Prospectively validated indicators and retained-revenue interventions |
+| `LF-T1/T2` | Tested product hypotheses, not feedback summarization |
+| `CS-T1/T2` | Materiality, scenarios, prediction tracking, and decision impact |
+| `SEO-T1/T2` | Separate or connect to causal commercial experiments |
+| `DW-T1/T2` | Use beneath governed engineering decisions |
+| `FH-CMS-001` | Contradiction, expiry-impact, evidence-quality, and lineage features |
+| `FH-SIGN-001` | Keep only as a governed-artifact add-on |
+| `firehorse-data-services` | Replace broad promise with a bounded data-to-decision product |
+| `devops-lead` | Publish scoring, evidence, sensitivity, baseline, and outcome |
+
+#### Strategic inconsistencies
+
+- `DWS-US-STARTER` and `DWS-US-PILOT` weaken the Sovereign Industrial Intelligence narrative. Keep only as explicitly non-sovereign evaluation tiers with mandatory migration paths.
+- Rewrite the DWS IQ Platform offer around audited decisions, CRC, evidence quality, and measured outcomes rather than fleet size, ontology-class count, captain hats, and an unsupported “90% reduction” headline.
+- The catalog has grown far beyond the Product Standard's historical “30-product rule.” Breadth now risks making DWS look like unrelated services rather than one compounding intelligence system.
+
+## 9. Recommended architecture
+
+1. **DWS IQ Intelligence Core** — governed decision engine, evidence graph, evaluation system, HIC controls, MGD/CRC.
+2. **Intelligence Functions** — Compliance, ESG, HSE, Construction, Sovereignty, Commercial/GTM, and Themis.
+3. **Industry Research Pods** — ontology, evaluations, regulatory models, and validated discoveries.
+4. **Deployment and Adoption** — sovereign cloud/edge, integrations, training, implementation, and signed evidence; never presented as the intelligence itself.
+
+> One intelligence core, multiple enterprise functions, industry-specific research depth, and optional sovereign deployment.
+
+## 10. First 90-day programme
+
+- **Days 1–30:** select one compliance, one operational/safety, and one commercial decision; assign owners; build 30–50 expert gold cases each; measure current baselines.
+- **Days 31–60:** implement evidence, assumptions, competing hypotheses, calibrated confidence, and audit replay; run repeatability, perturbation, cross-model, and expert-review tests.
+- **Days 61–90:** identify one high-value unknown per workflow; design a test or prospective prediction; validate at least one hypothesis; convert it into customer-owned ontology/evaluation capital; publish a redacted Evidence Room.
+
+## 11. Success criteria
+
+The strategy works when MGD and CRC grow; evidence coverage and calibration improve; unsupported claims and overrides decline; cycle time and review effort fall; at least one validated discovery per quarter changes an enterprise decision; and core recurring revenue grows faster than stand-alone services.
+
+It is not working if growth is explained mainly by more agents, SKUs, pilots, model calls, or consulting hours.
+
+## 12. HIC decision point
+
+**Q1 — Portfolio gate (RECOMMEND: APPROVE)**  
+**Decision owner:** Risto Anton Päärni, Founder, CEO (R22)  
+**Reversibility:** Two-way door; revise after quarterly evidence.  
+**Verified basis:** Current catalog, MGD/CRC doctrine, and sources below.  
+**Proposed action:** From Q4 2026, no offer headlines DWS IQ Intelligence unless it passes Level 3. Level 4–5 claims require an evaluation card and independent review. Other offers are labeled Deployment, Adoption, Infrastructure, or Services.  
+**Answer format:** `Q1 APPROVE` or `Q1 REJECT — <reason>`.
+
+## Sources
+
+1. NIST AI RMF and Generative AI Profile: https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework
+2. Stanford HAI, 2025 AI Index — Economy: https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/economy
+3. Stanford HAI, 2025 AI Index — Responsible AI: https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report/responsible-ai
+4. McKinsey, State of AI 2025: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai
+5. European Commission AI Act Service Desk, Articles 12 and 14: https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-12 and https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-14
+6. OECD, AI in policy evaluation: https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/governing-with-artificial-intelligence_795de142-en/full-report/ai-in-policy-evaluation_c88cc2fd.html
+7. Internal sources: `DWS_TRUTH_STANDARD.md`, `DWS_PRODUCT_STANDARD.md`, `DWS_MARKET_RESEARCH_STANDARD.md`, `DWS_ROLES_REGISTRY.md`, `AI_AGENT_GUIDELINES.md`, `config/truth/mgd-crc-metrics.json`, and `dws10.com/config/products.json`.

+

+

#!/bin/bash
# Sender-identity guard — PreToolUse for Write/Edit tools
# Blocks any draft that uses the wrong spelling or wrong title for the sender.
# Exit 0 = ALLOW, Exit 2 = BLOCK
#
# Canonical sender per CLAUDE.md and skills/signature/SKILL.md:
#   Name : Risto Anton Päärni  (umlauts on BOTH a's)
#   Title: Founder, CEO
#   Phone: +358 400 319 010
#
# Rationale: after multiple sessions producing "Risto Paarni / CEO, Lifetime Oy"
# we lock the canonical form at the hook layer so future sessions cannot drift.
# Code-Version: 1.0 | Branch: claude/b3b-outreach-analysis-7AtlA | Date: 2026-05-11

INPUT=$(cat)

json_get() {
  key="$1"
  default="${2:-}"
  if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r ".${key} // \"$default\"" 2>/dev/null
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s' "$default"
}

TOOL_NAME=$(json_get "tool_name" "")
FILE_PATH=$(json_get "tool_input.file_path" "")
CONTENT=$(json_get "tool_input.content" "")
NEW_STRING=$(json_get "tool_input.new_string" "")

# Combine the payload we will scan
PAYLOAD="${CONTENT}${NEW_STRING}"

# Only guard Write/Edit operations
case "$TOOL_NAME" in
  Write|Edit|MultiEdit) ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac

# Skip if no payload
[ -z "$PAYLOAD" ] && exit 0

# Allowlist: files that legitimately document the anti-pattern.
# These contain the literal string "Paarni" as something to scan FOR, not produce.
case "$FILE_PATH" in
  */.claude/hooks/check-signature.sh) exit 0 ;;
  */skills/signature/SKILL.md) exit 0 ;;
  */outreach/LESSONS.md) exit 0 ;;
  */CLAUDE.md) exit 0 ;;
  */CLAUDE.local.md) exit 0 ;;
esac

# Determine scope: external-facing artifacts where signature correctness matters.
# Always scan: outreach/, emails, intros, signatures, anything with a sig block.
SCOPE_MATCH=0
case "$FILE_PATH" in
  */outreach/*|*/email_*|*/email-*|*/INTRO_*|*/signature/*|*/skills/signature/*) SCOPE_MATCH=1 ;;
esac

# Also scan if payload contains tell-tale signature scaffolding
if echo "$PAYLOAD" | grep -qE '(Lifetime Oy|risto\.paarni@lifetime\.fi|Founder, CEO|Risto Anton)'; then
  SCOPE_MATCH=1
fi

[ "$SCOPE_MATCH" -eq 0 ] && exit 0

AUDIT_DIR=".claude/hooks/audit"
mkdir -p "$AUDIT_DIR"

block() {
  REASON="$1"
  HINT="$2"
  echo "$(date -Iseconds) BLOCKED check-signature: $REASON file=$FILE_PATH" >> "$AUDIT_DIR/check-signature.log"
  cat >&2 <<EOF
BLOCKED: Sender-identity violation in $FILE_PATH

Problem: $REASON

Canonical (from skills/signature/SKILL.md):
  Risto Anton Päärni       (umlauts on BOTH a's — Päärni, NOT Paarni)
  Founder, CEO             (comma form, NOT "CEO" alone, NOT "Founder & CEO")
  Lifetime Oy
  risto.paarni@lifetime.fi
  +358 400 319 010

Fix hint: $HINT
EOF
  exit 2
}

# Rule 1: name without umlauts
if echo "$PAYLOAD" | grep -qE '(^|[^ä])Paarni'; then
  # allow inside the email handle "risto.paarni@lifetime.fi"
  STRIPPED=$(echo "$PAYLOAD" | sed -E 's/risto\.paarni@lifetime\.fi//g')
  if echo "$STRIPPED" | grep -qE '(^|[^ä])Paarni'; then
    block \
      'Found "Paarni" (no umlauts) outside the email handle.' \
      'Replace with "Päärni" (umlauts on both a). The email handle risto.paarni@lifetime.fi is the only ASCII-correct occurrence.'
  fi
fi

# Rule 2: "Päarni" (one umlaut only) — common middle-state error
if echo "$PAYLOAD" | grep -qE 'Päarni|Paärni'; then
  block \
    'Found "Päarni" or "Paärni" (one umlaut only).' \
    'Both a-letters carry the umlaut: Päärni.'
fi

# Rule 3: title missing "Founder," — only check when "Lifetime Oy" appears in a sig-like context
if echo "$PAYLOAD" | grep -qE 'Lifetime Oy'; then
  if echo "$PAYLOAD" | grep -qE 'CEO[, ·]+Lifetime Oy' && ! echo "$PAYLOAD" | grep -qE 'Founder, CEO'; then
    block \
      'Found "CEO, Lifetime Oy" (or similar) without "Founder,".' \
      'Use "Founder, CEO · Lifetime Oy" or "Founder, CEO\nLifetime Oy".'
  fi
fi

# Rule 4: "CEO & Founder" / "Founder & CEO" in signature-structured fields
if echo "$PAYLOAD" | grep -qE '(CEO[[:space:]]*&[[:space:]]*Founder|CEO and Founder)'; then
  block \
    'Found reversed/conjoined title form ("CEO & Founder" or "CEO and Founder").' \
    'Canonical title is "Founder, CEO" (comma form). The byline-only exception "Founder & CEO" is allowed inside publication prose, never in signature blocks.'
fi

exit 0

     if printf '%s' "$COMMAND" | grep -qiE '^(env|printenv)([[:space:]]+(-[a-z0-9]+|[A-Z_]*(KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASS|PASSWORD|PASSPHRASE|CREDENTIAL)[A-Z_]*))*[[:space:]]*($|[|>])'; then
       block "Bare environment dump ('$FIRST_TOKEN') is not allowed — it exposes every secret. Reference a specific non-secret var instead."
     fi
     ;;
 esac
 
 # ── SAFE COMMANDS: allow immediately, skip all deny checks ────────────────────
 # These commands may contain arbitrary string content (commit messages,
 # inline scripts) that would false-positive on deny patterns.
 case "$FIRST_TOKEN" in
   node|npx|npm|tsx|vitest|jest|prettier|eslint) exit 0 ;;  # JS tooling
   python|python3|pip|pip3|ruff|black|bandit) exit 0 ;;     # Python tooling
   make|cargo|go|rustc) exit 0 ;;                            # Build tools
   ls|pwd|echo|cat|head|tail|wc|file|which|type) exit 0 ;;  # Read-only
   find|grep|rg|diff|tree|du|df|date|env|printenv) exit 0 ;; # Inspect
   mkdir|touch|cp|mv|chmod|tar|zip|unzip) exit 0 ;;          # File ops (safe after pre-check above)
   docker|docker-compose|gh|jq|curl|wget) exit 0 ;;          # Tools
   SKIP_TIME_CHECK=*|CLAUDE_*|NODE_ENV=*) exit 0 ;;          # Env-prefixed
 esac
 
 # Also allow env-var-prefixed commands (VAR=value command ...)
 if printf '%s' "$COMMAND" | grep -qE '^[A-Z_]+=[^ ]+ (node|npx|npm|tsx|python)'; then
   exit 0
 fi
 
 # ── DENY LIST: destructive patterns ──────────────────────────────────────────
 
 # ── Delete / destroy operations ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 # rm -rf and rm -fr: block on ALL paths (absolute and relative).
 # Exception: /tmp/ paths are safe.
 case "$FIRST_TOKEN" in
   rm)
     # ALL rm is blocked — no file deletions allowed.
     # The only permitted removal method is renaming to _OLD (git mv <file> <file_OLD.ext>).
     # Exception: /tmp/ paths (build artifacts, temp files).
